name: Conflict-Check Engine

parameters.content:
## Conflict-Check Engine

### How it works

1. The workflow triggers upon receiving a conflict check request via webhook and processes the input names to validate them.
2. If valid, it retrieves firm contacts and matters from Clio, runs a fuzzy match to detect possible conflicts, and logs this check for audit with a generated check ID.
3. It builds and sends a styled conflict report email containing decision links to compliance.
4. On receiving a conflict decision via a separate webhook, it validates the request and looks up the corresponding audit log.
5. Based on the lookup, it updates the conflict check record with the decision or responds with errors if invalid.
6. Responses and confirmations are sent back through webhooks to complete each request cycle.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure and deploy webhook URLs correctly for both conflict check requests and conflict decisions.
- [ ] Add and configure Clio API credentials and set the CLIO_BASE_URL environment variable.
- [ ] Set up Google Sheets credentials with access to the audit log sheet.
- [ ] Configure an email provider credential for sending conflict report emails.

### Customization

Customize the fuzzy matching sensitivity to balance false positives and negatives. Adjust email templates and add more detailed logging as needed.

## Trigger and parse conflict request

Receives the initial conflict check webhook request, parses submitted names, and validates the request format.

## Fetch contacts and matters from Clio

Retrieves all firm contacts and matters from Clio APIs to support conflict matching, executed only after request validation.

## Run conflict matching and assign ID

Runs the fuzzy matching algorithm to detect conflicts and generates a stable conflict check ID for audit consistency.

## Audit logging of conflict check

Logs the conflict check data into Google Sheets for audit purposes, linking all details with the assigned check ID.

## Build and send report email

Constructs a formatted email report with decision links and sends it to compliance contacts.

## Trigger and parse decision request

Receives conflict decision webhook requests and parses the decision data to prepare for validation.

## Read and validate conflict check log

Reads the Google Sheets audit log and matches the decision's check ID to an existing record, directing flow based on existence.

## Update log with decision and respond

Updates the existing conflict check record with the decision outcome and responds with a confirmation page to the requester.

nodes.name: Conflict Check Request Trigger
nodes.notes: Wire this to whatever staff use before opening a matter — a Fluent Forms conflict-check form is the simplest option. Expects: new_client_name, adverse_party_names (comma-separated), matter_description, requested_by_email.

nodes.name: Parse Conflict Check Names
nodes.notes: At least one name is required — the new client's name alone is enough to run a check, adverse parties are optional extras.

nodes.name: If Conflict Request Valid
nodes.notes: True continues to run the actual match; false means the submission had no names at all and just gets acknowledged.

nodes.name: Respond Invalid Conflict Request
nodes.notes: Acknowledges an empty/malformed submission rather than silently doing nothing.

nodes.name: Fetch All Contacts From Clio
nodes.notes: Every contact in Clio — clients, related parties, everyone — is fair game for a conflict match. Firms with over 200 contacts need pagination added (not built here).

nodes.name: Fetch All Matters From Clio
nodes.notes: Deliberately not filtered by status -- a closed matter's adverse party is still a real conflict risk years later. Solo/small firms won't hit the 200-matter cap; larger ones will need pagination added.

nodes.name: Run Fuzzy Match On Conflicts
nodes.notes: The whole matching engine lives here. CONFLICT_MATCH_THRESHOLD (0-1) controls sensitivity — lower catches more names at the cost of more false positives; this tool is meant to over-surface, not under-surface.

nodes.name: Generate Stable Conflict Check ID
nodes.notes: This ID is what ties the audit log row to whichever decision link the attorney eventually clicks.

nodes.name: Append Conflict Check To Audit
nodes.notes: Every conflict check gets a permanent audit row here, regardless of whether anything matched — being able to prove a check was run is as important as the result itself. Column headers must match exactly.

nodes.name: Build Styled Conflict Report Email
nodes.notes: CONFLICT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL must be set to this workflow's own Production URL for 'When Conflict Decision Is Made' — copy it after activating. Reads deal fields back from 'Assign Conflict Check ID' by name, not $json, since the Sheets append node in between echoes back a flattened row, not the original structured data.

nodes.name: Trigger Compliance Audit Workflow
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget audit logging only — this goes to firm staff, not a client, so the guardrail's approval result is deliberately ignored, same internal-notification pattern used throughout this catalog.

nodes.name: Send Conflict Report Email
nodes.notes: Reaches back to 'Build Conflict Report Email' by name, not $json, since the guardrail call in between replaces $json with its own response.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { status: 'submitted', check_id: $('Generate Stable Conflict Check ID').item.json.check_id } }}

nodes.name: Respond Conflict Check Submission
nodes.notes: Acknowledges the original submission — staff get the check_id back immediately, the full report follows by email.

nodes.name: Conflict Decision Request Trigger
nodes.notes: This is the URL the two links in the report email point to — copy its Production URL into CONFLICT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL after activating.

nodes.name: Parse Conflict Decision Request
nodes.notes: Pulls check_id and action (clear/escalate) out of the query string and validates both are present.

nodes.name: If Conflict Decision Valid
nodes.notes: True continues to look up the check; false means the link is malformed or missing a required parameter.

nodes.name: Respond Invalid Conflict Decision
nodes.notes: Plain error page for a malformed or incomplete decision link.

nodes.name: Read Conflict Check Audit Log
nodes.notes: Reads every logged conflict check so the specific one referenced by check_id can be found.

nodes.name: Find Matching Audit Log Row
nodes.notes: Matches the decision link's check_id against the audit log by exact string equality — confirmed live via raw JSON output that stored values carry no whitespace.

nodes.name: If Conflict Check Found
nodes.notes: True continues to record the decision; false means the check_id doesn't match any logged row (already resolved, or a malformed link).

parameters.responseBody: We couldn't find that conflict check — it may have already been resolved or the link is malformed.

nodes.name: Respond Conflict Check Not Found
nodes.notes: Plain error page — nothing in the log gets changed when this fires.

nodes.name: Update Conflict Check With Decision
nodes.notes: Uses Append or Update (not plain Update Row) matching on check_id -- plain Update Row was silently matching zero rows despite the check_id, header, and sheet all being confirmed correct live. If a row with this check_id exists it's updated in place; there is no code path anywhere in this workflow that opens, blocks, or auto-approves a matter based on this.

parameters.responseBody:
={{ '

' + ($('Find Matching Audit Log Row').item.json.action === 'clear' ? '✅ Marked cleared' : '🔺 Marked for escalation') + '

Recorded for ' + $('Find Matching Audit Log Row').item.json.names_checked + '.

nodes.name: Respond Conflict Decision Confirmation
nodes.notes: Reads action/names_checked back from 'Find Matching Conflict Check Row' by name, not $json -- the Sheets update node in between echoes back its own written row (check_id/status/decision/decided_at only), which doesn't include either field. No further automated action happens after this.

json.names_checked: Jon Smyth, Acme Corporation, Maria Jonas

description: Runs on two independent webhooks. Conflict check: fuzzy-matches every submitted name (new client plus known adverse parties) against every Clio contact and every matter's client name and description, logs the check and its results to an audit sheet, and emails the requesting attorney a report with Clear/Escalate decision links. Decision: records whichever link was clicked in the audit log. Never clears or blocks a matter automatically -- the attorney always makes the actual conflict determination (ABA Op. 512). Replaces manual conflict checks and PM add-ons, catching matches a manual review misses.
